def reset_schema_ready_flags():
    """Forget which tables have been provisioned/verified.

    These latches are module-level globals, so they outlive the per-test
    database rollback that drops the SQLite tables they refer to. A test class
    that reset only some of them would leave the rest claiming a table exists
    after it had been rolled away, and the next request path to touch that
    table failed with "no such table" depending purely on test order. Tests
    call this in setUp so provisioning state always matches the live schema.
    """
    globals().update({name: False for name in _SCHEMA_READY_FLAGS})
    cache_state._CURRICULUM_EPOCH_TABLE_READY = False
    reset_learner_schema_cache()
    # The notification ledger keeps its own latch, in its own module, for the
    # same reason as the ones above.
    tutor_notifications._TABLE_READY = False
    # Review templates likewise -- reviews.py is a sibling module with its own
    # latch, deferred-imported here to avoid a module-load-time circular import
    # (reviews.py imports this module).
    from . import reviews as _reviews
    _reviews._REVIEW_TABLES_READY = False
    from . import review_schedule as _review_schedule
    _review_schedule._REVIEW_SCHEDULE_TABLES_READY = False
    from . import review_types as _review_types
    _review_types.reset_ready_flag()
    from . import review_instances as _review_instances
    _review_instances._TABLES_READY = False
    _review_instances._MANUAL_OVERRIDES_TABLE_READY = False
    _review_instances._LEARNER_REVIEW_ADDITIONS_TABLE_READY = False
    _TABLE_COLUMNS_CACHE.clear()
    from .catalogue.infrastructure import database_reads
    database_reads._TABLE_COLUMNS_LISTED = False
    _TABLE_EXISTS_CACHE.clear()
    schema_gate.reset_verification_cache()

def component_text_cancels(items, identity_fields, *, clean_str, normalise):
    """Whether unique_curriculum_items() decides the same with or without text.

    Its richness is ``len(json.dumps(item))`` plus counts that do not involve
    text. Where every candidate sharing a key carries the very same components
    -- the same rows, built by the same code -- each component's text adds the
    same length to both sides of every comparison it makes, so blanking it
    changes no decision. Any key whose candidates carry different components,
    or components not built from the shared rows, makes this False, and the
    caller reads the text after all. Keys mirror unique_curriculum_items(); an
    item it gives a row key of its own is never compared.
    """
    layouts = defaultdict(set)
    for item in items or []:
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            continue
        key = next((clean_str(item.get(field)) for field in identity_fields if clean_str(item.get(field))), '')
        if not key:
            key = normalise(item.get('name') or item.get('title'))
        if not key:
            continue
        layout = _component_layout(item)
        if layout is None:
            return False
        layouts[key].add(layout)
    return all(len(found) == 1 for found in layouts.values())

def enabled(db=connection, *, refresh=False):
    if db.vendor != 'postgresql':
        return False
    key = (db.alias, db.settings_dict.get('HOST'), db.settings_dict.get('PORT'), db.settings_dict.get('NAME'))
    if not refresh and key in _ready:
        return _ready[key]
    if not refresh and monotonic() < _not_ready_until.get(key, 0):
        return False
    required_values = ','.join(['(%s,%s)'] * len(NATIVE_REQUIRED_COLUMNS))
    required_params = [value for pair in NATIVE_REQUIRED_COLUMNS for value in pair]
    with db.cursor() as cursor:
        cursor.execute(f"""WITH required_columns(table_name,column_name) AS (
                VALUES {required_values}
            ), required_views(view_name) AS (
                SELECT unnest(%s::text[])
            )
            SELECT
                NOT EXISTS (
                    SELECT 1 FROM required_columns required
                    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
                        SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns actual
                        WHERE actual.table_schema='curriculum'
                          AND actual.table_name=required.table_name
                          AND actual.column_name=required.column_name
                    )
                )
                AND NOT EXISTS (
                    SELECT 1 FROM required_views required
                    WHERE to_regclass('curriculum.' || required.view_name) IS NULL
                )""", [*required_params, list(NATIVE_VIEWS.values())])
        ready = cursor.fetchone()[0]
    # A worker may have answered requests before the coordinated cutover.
    # Never keep that negative result for its entire lifetime: after migration
    # it must see the native tables without falling back to ordinary modules.
    if ready is True:
        _ready[key] = True
        _not_ready_until.pop(key, None)
    else:
        _ready.pop(key, None)
        # Keep catalogue reads inexpensive on a database awaiting cutover.
        _not_ready_until[key] = monotonic() + 5
    return ready is True

def ensure_module_authoring_tables():
    """Verify the module-authoring tables exist.

    Schema is owned by migrations. In production this is a cached read-only
    probe that raises SchemaNotProvisioned if a table is missing; it never
    creates or alters anything. Test/local runs delegate to the provisioning
    path below, which still owns the DDL.
    """
    global _AUTHORING_TABLES_READY
    if native_only():
        schema_gate.require_tables('free_courses', 'free_course_weeks', 'free_programme_components')
        return
    if _AUTHORING_TABLES_READY:
        return
    if not schema_gate.runtime_bootstrap_allowed():
        schema_gate.require_tables(*AUTHORING_REQUIRED_TABLES)
        _AUTHORING_TABLES_READY = True
        return
    provision_module_authoring_tables()

def reset_schema_ready_flags():
    """Forget which tables have been provisioned/verified.

    These latches are module-level globals, so they outlive the per-test
    database rollback that drops the SQLite tables they refer to. A test class
    that reset only some of them would leave the rest claiming a table exists
    after it had been rolled away, and the next request path to touch that
    table failed with "no such table" depending purely on test order. Tests
    call this in setUp so provisioning state always matches the live schema.
    """
    globals().update({name: False for name in _SCHEMA_READY_FLAGS})
    cache_state._CURRICULUM_EPOCH_TABLE_READY = False
    reset_learner_schema_cache()
    # The notification ledger keeps its own latch, in its own module, for the
    # same reason as the ones above.
    tutor_notifications._TABLE_READY = False
    # Review templates likewise -- reviews.py is a sibling module with its own
    # latch, deferred-imported here to avoid a module-load-time circular import
    # (reviews.py imports this module).
    from . import reviews as _reviews
    _reviews._REVIEW_TABLES_READY = False
    from . import review_schedule as _review_schedule
    _review_schedule._REVIEW_SCHEDULE_TABLES_READY = False
    from . import review_types as _review_types
    _review_types.reset_ready_flag()
    from . import review_instances as _review_instances
    _review_instances._TABLES_READY = False
    _review_instances._MANUAL_OVERRIDES_TABLE_READY = False
    _review_instances._LEARNER_REVIEW_ADDITIONS_TABLE_READY = False
    _TABLE_COLUMNS_CACHE.clear()
    from .catalogue.infrastructure import database_reads
    database_reads._TABLE_COLUMNS_LISTED = False
    _TABLE_EXISTS_CACHE.clear()
    schema_gate.reset_verification_cache()

def component_text_cancels(items, identity_fields, *, clean_str, normalise):
    """Whether unique_curriculum_items() decides the same with or without text.

    Its richness is ``len(json.dumps(item))`` plus counts that do not involve
    text. Where every candidate sharing a key carries the very same components
    -- the same rows, built by the same code -- each component's text adds the
    same length to both sides of every comparison it makes, so blanking it
    changes no decision. Any key whose candidates carry different components,
    or components not built from the shared rows, makes this False, and the
    caller reads the text after all. Keys mirror unique_curriculum_items(); an
    item it gives a row key of its own is never compared.
    """
    layouts = defaultdict(set)
    for item in items or []:
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            continue
        key = next((clean_str(item.get(field)) for field in identity_fields if clean_str(item.get(field))), '')
        if not key:
            key = normalise(item.get('name') or item.get('title'))
        if not key:
            continue
        layout = _component_layout(item)
        if layout is None:
            return False
        layouts[key].add(layout)
    return all(len(found) == 1 for found in layouts.values())
